pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/errorline/ErrorLine.tsx:12 A live ErrorLine owns its own role=alert region, mounted together with its message (callers do `{refusal !== null && <ErrorLine message={refusal} live />}`). It bypasses the shell announcer (lib/announcer.tsx rules 1-2), and an identical refusal on retry makes no DOM change, so it is not voiced a second time.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/errorline/ErrorLine.tsx:12 The primitive owns a region instead of asking the one provider. The region arrives with its text, and repeats have no re-announce mechanism. Many pairings voice an inserted alert, which softens rule 1 but not one-writer or repeats.

packages/ui/test/components/signal.test.ts:140 The test asserts that the live-region attribute is present, which is the proxy the gate-sees-target trap names. No voiced sequence or repeat is asserted.

packages/ui/src/components/hint/Hint.module.css:11 The closed tip is `visibility:hidden` (line 8) and flips with opacity from the same data-open condition, so both channels close together. It is still referenced by aria-describedby, which is allowed. This resolves the earlier stale verdict.
packages/ui/src/components/hint/Hint.tsx:37 The icon-only '?' glyph has a REQUIRED name prop, and its tip is wired as the description. Glyph SVGs are aria-hidden throughout Glyph.tsx.

packages/ui/src/components/ghost/Ghost.tsx:14 A meaning drawn only as an outline is put back on the element as a spoken label. The outlines are aria-hidden, and the label is required by the prop type.

packages/ui/src/components/chip/Chip.module.css:13 The ghost mark is held to 3:1 non-text contrast, mixed from the text colour so tones keep the floor. The hover state is handled the same way on line 20.
